findings.title: Stop() no longer rejects RPCs, so writes accepted after shutdown never reach watchers or the search index
findings.description:
Before this change every RPC called `s.Init(ctx)`, which returns `s.initErr` once the `once` has run. `Stop()` sets `s.initErr` to "service is stopping" and then "service is stopped" (server.go:321, 339), so those RPCs returned an error after shutdown. The diff removes that call from Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob and GetBlob. `initErr` is now read only in `Init` (server.go:317), which runs once inside the constructor (server.go:258), so no RPC checks the stopped state anymore.

The effect is concrete for the SQL backend. After `Stop()`, `WriteEvent` (sql/backend.go:157) still commits. `Stop()` calls the backend's `cancel` (backend.go:120), which closes the `done` channel (backend.go:56-57), and the poller returns on `<-b.done` (backend.go:577-578). The event is never published to watchers or the search index, and the caller gets success instead of "service is stopped". Nothing under `pkg/` calls `ResourceServer.Stop` today, so the impact is latent, but the shutdown contract the code encodes no longer holds. A fix is an explicit stopped check at the top of these RPCs, or a shared helper, that returns `s.initErr` when it is set.

findings.title: Removing cacheMu from BuildIndex lets concurrent builds of the same key overwrite each other, dropping writes made to the superseded index
findings.description:
The diff drops the `cacheMu.Lock()` that covered all of `BuildIndex` and keeps it only around the store at lines 137-139, which writes `b.cache[key] = idx` unconditionally. Nothing else serializes builds for the same key. `getOrCreateIndex` (resource/search.go:287-307) has only a TODO (lines 288-290) saying it should block per key. Two paths reach it concurrently: the Search RPC (server.go:920 → search.go:148) and `handleEvent` (search.go:237).

With the default `index_file_threshold` of 10 (setting_unified_storage.go:44), `getOrCreateIndex`'s size of 10 gives a memory index, so both builds succeed. Trace: Search starts build A and reads storage. A create event for the same key commits and is handled. Build B completes and is cached, and `handleEvent` writes the document into B (search.go:257). Then A finishes and replaces B at bleve.go:138. The document is missing from the cached index until restart or another event.

Before the change, the global lock ran builds one at a time, so each later build started after the earlier one had published and read committed state. The removal probably aims to let init builds run in parallel, which `group.SetLimit(s.initWorkers)` (search.go:179) suggests was intended but the global lock prevented. That needs a per-key guard, such as a per-key mutex or singleflight in `getOrCreateIndex`, rather than removing the global lock.
